adults.title: Credentials for the Journey Home
adults.big_idea: Covenants kept over time are sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise, and no one else's unrighteous choices can take God's promised blessings from a faithful covenant keeper.
adults.objective: Learners will explain in their own words what it means for a covenant to be sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise and will choose one way to hold fast to their covenants this week.
prepare: Read Elder Bednar's talk, Sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise, and mark the sections The Parable of the Passport, The Holy Ghost Is the Holy Spirit of Promise, and The Sealing Ordinance.
Ask class members to have the talk open in Gospel Library, or bring a few printed copies.
Bring paper and pens for silent writing.
Write on the board: repent sincerely and consistently / honor our covenants / yield our hearts unto God.
Pray for those in the room who have been hurt by another person's choices. Decide now that you will not ask anyone to describe a marriage or family situation.

segments.name: What gets you through the gate?
steps: Begin with prayer. Then ask everyone to think of a document they guard carefully: a passport, a license, a birth certificate.
In pairs, give one minute each to answer the first question below.

Tell the class that Elder Bednar began his talk with words he learned from President Boyd K. Packer. Read President Packer's sentence from the aligned quotes and ask the second question. Take two or three answers.
questions: What makes that document worth protecting, and what would you lose if it were damaged?
President Packer called ordinances and covenants credentials. What do you think he wanted us to feel about them?

segments.name: The parable of the passport
steps: Form groups of three or four. Ask each group to read the section The Parable of the Passport together.
Give the groups two things to find: what the man had, and what he had not done.
Bring the class back and hear a short report from two groups.

Ask someone to read the last paragraph of that section aloud, where Elder Bednar names the limit of his analogy. Make sure the class hears it clearly: hardship that comes through no fault of our own does not diminish God's promises to us or invalidate our covenants.
questions: The man held a valid passport and was still turned away. What is Elder Bednar teaching about receiving a covenant and keeping it?
Why do you think Elder Bednar stopped to say what his story does not mean?

segments.name: The stamp: sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise
steps: Invite everyone to read silently the section The Holy Ghost Is the Holy Spirit of Promise, and then Doctrine and Covenants 132:7. Ask them to notice what the Holy Ghost does with our ordinances and covenants.
Ask a class member to read aloud the key quote that begins with the words Receiving this ratifying sealing.

Point to the three phrases on the board. Give two minutes of silent writing: which of these three is the Lord inviting me to give more attention to right now, and what would that look like on an ordinary weekday?
Invite a few to share what they are willing to share. Note the phrase “in process of time” from Moses 7:21, which Elder Bednar uses for how this seal is received.
questions: What changes for you when you think of this sealing as something that comes over time and not as a single event?
How have you seen steady, repeated repentance strengthen your confidence before God?

segments.name: When another person's choices bring sorrow
steps: Say gently that the next section speaks to a tender question, and that no one will be asked to share a personal situation.

Ask one person to read aloud the two parts of the sealing ordinance that Elder Bednar describes in the section The Sealing Ordinance. Then ask another to read the paragraph that begins Sometimes, unfortunately, through the end of that section, slowly.
Ask the class to listen for two lists: what Elder Bednar says he does not know, and what he says he does know. Write both on the board in the class's words.
Read Doctrine and Covenants 64:31–32 together and ask what it adds about the Lord's promises and His timing.
Share Elder Hathaway's sentence from the aligned quotes and ask the questions below.
questions: Elder Bednar is honest that revealed doctrine does not answer every detail. How does his testimony of what he does know help you live with questions that are not yet answered?
What does it mean to you that the Savior's Atonement can overcome all things for every person who holds fast to their covenants with Him?

segments.name: King Benjamin's promise
steps: Read Mosiah 2:41 aloud together from the scriptures. Elder Bednar closed his talk with this verse.
Check for understanding: ask each person to turn to a neighbor and finish this sentence in their own words: A covenant is sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise when…
Listen in on two or three pairs. If you hear the idea of a one-time event, return briefly to the three phrases on the board.
questions: Which word in King Benjamin's promise do you most need today?

segments.name: Choose and act
steps: Elder Bednar did not give a specific assignment in this talk, so invite each person to decide prayerfully how to act on what he taught. Show the ideas in the act list and give one quiet minute to write a choice.
Bear your testimony that promised blessings will be received by those who hold fast to their covenants with the Savior.
Follow up: tell the class you will begin next week by asking what they noticed as they acted. Next week, give the first two minutes to that question.

key_quotes.text: Ongoing faithfulness is required for those credentials to be valid and for promised blessings to be received.

Receiving this ratifying sealing by the Holy Ghost typically is not a one-time event; rather, it comes over time as we repent sincerely and consistently, honor our covenants, and yield our hearts unto God.
The power of the Lord’s infinite and eternal Atonement can overcome all things, all the time, everywhere, for every person who holds fast to their covenants with Him.
No faithful disciple will ultimately be deprived of any eternal blessing God has promised because of another individual’s unrighteous exercise of moral agency.

scriptures.use: Read silently after the section on the Holy Spirit of Promise. Find the words Elder Bednar quotes and ask what the verse says must happen to every covenant.
Point out the phrase “in process of time,” which Elder Bednar uses to describe how the ratifying seal is received. Ask what that phrase teaches about patience with ourselves.
Read together after the section The Sealing Ordinance. Ask what these verses teach about the certainty of the Lord's promises and about His timing.
Read aloud together near the end. Invite each person to choose one word from King Benjamin's promise that they need today.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Boyd K. Packer
aligned_quotes.text: Ordinances and covenants become our credentials for admission into His presence. To worthily receive them is the quest of a lifetime; to keep them thereafter is the challenge of mortality.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Hathaway
aligned_quotes.text: the question for most righteous followers is not if He will deliver but how and when He will do so

takeaways: Receiving a covenant opens the way; keeping it over time is how its blessings come.
The Holy Ghost seals our covenants as we repent consistently, honor them, and yield our hearts to God.
No one else's unrighteous choices can take from me what God has promised.
act: Each night this week, ask in prayer what you can repent of today, and act on the first thing that comes.
Before the sacrament on Sunday, read Mosiah 2:41 and tell Heavenly Father one covenant you want to honor more fully.
If another person's choices have brought you sorrow, write the key quote that begins No faithful disciple where you will see it each morning.
Schedule a time to worship in the house of the Lord, or take one step toward being ready to go.
adapt: At home or with two or three people: skip the groups. Read the passport story aloud, then the paragraph that begins Sometimes, unfortunately, and talk through the two lists together.
Large class: keep people in pairs for every discussion so that everyone speaks, and take only two reports each time.
Short on time: teach the passport segment, the three phrases on the board, and the key quote that begins No faithful disciple, then go straight to choosing an action.

youth.title: Will It Get You In?
youth.big_idea: A covenant is an enduring promise between God and me; as I keep it over time the Holy Ghost seals it, and no one else's choices can take God's blessings from me.
youth.objective: Youth will be able to explain what a covenant is and how the Holy Ghost seals it over time, and will choose one daily way to take care of their covenants this week.
prepare: Read Elder Bednar's talk, Sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise.
Ask youth to bring phones or scriptures; they will open the talk in Gospel Library.
Bring paper, pens, and a few markers for the board.
Write three words across the board with space under each: REPENT, HONOR, YIELD.
Some youth live with the pain of a family member's choices. Plan to teach the last part gently and do not ask anyone about their family.

segments.name: Will it get you in?
steps: Start right after the prayer. Say: stand if this would get you in, stay seated if it would not.

Call out quickly: a concert ticket for last year's show. A school ID that went through the wash and cannot be read. A library card with someone else's name on it. A valid boarding pass for today's flight.
Ask the first question below and take three fast answers.
Tell them Elder Bednar taught that ordinances and covenants are spiritual credentials for our journey home to Heavenly Father.
questions: What has to be true about a ticket or an ID for it to actually work?

segments.name: The passport story
steps: Choose a traveler, a border official, and a narrator. The narrator reads the section The Parable of the Passport from a phone, stopping before the paragraph that begins The lesson of this story, while the other two act it out without words.
Ask everyone to read silently the last two paragraphs of that section.
Ask the questions below. Be sure the youth hear Elder Bednar's own caution: hard things that happen to us through no fault of our own do not damage our covenants or God's promises.
questions: The passport was real and valid. Why was that not enough?
Elder Bednar says his story has limits. What does he not want anyone to conclude from it?

segments.name: Twelve-word challenge
steps: Phones face down. In teams of two or three, give 90 seconds to write the best definition of a covenant in twelve words or fewer.

Have each team read theirs aloud. Then have everyone open the section Covenants, Ordinances, and Promised Blessings and find Elder Bednar's definition. The team that came closest gets a round of applause.
Ask the teams to search the same section for two more answers: who sets the conditions of a covenant, and what our part is.
Ask a youth to read the key quote that begins A covenant is a solemn promise.
questions: Why does it matter that God sets the conditions and that we choose with our agency to accept them?
Which ordinances have you received so far, and which are still ahead of you?

segments.name: The stamp
steps: Explain that the traveler needed an official stamp. Elder Bednar compares that stamp to the witness of the Holy Ghost, whom the scriptures also call the Holy Spirit of Promise.
Read together the section The Holy Ghost Is the Holy Spirit of Promise. Then read Doctrine and Covenants 132:7 and have the youth find the words Elder Bednar quotes from it.
Ask a youth to read the key quote that begins Receiving this ratifying sealing. Point to REPENT, HONOR, YIELD on the board.
Hand out markers. Everyone comes up and writes under at least one word what it looks like on a normal Tuesday. Read a few aloud.
Read Doctrine and Covenants 136:4 and ask what walking in the ordinances of the Lord looks like in a school week. Then share President Packer's words from the aligned quotes.
questions: Elder Bednar says this sealing typically is not a one-time event. How does that change the way you think about a bad day or a mistake?
What is the difference between receiving an ordinance and keeping the covenant that comes with it?

segments.name: An honest question
steps: Say that Elder Bednar then spoke about the sealing of a husband and wife in the house of the Lord, and about what happens when one spouse breaks covenants. He voiced the question a faithful person might ask. Read the question and his answer from the key quotes or from the paragraph that begins Sometimes, unfortunately.
Read the key quote about what unrighteousness by one person cannot do. Explain that Elder Bednar taught this about marriage, and that his words reach every faithful disciple.
Point out his honesty: he says he does not know exactly how and when the blessings come, and that he does know they will come. Share Sister Runia's sentence from the aligned quotes.
Give two minutes of silent writing on the question below. No one shares unless they want to.
questions: When someone else's choices have hurt you or someone you love, what would you want to remember from Elder Bednar's testimony?

segments.name: Take care of your passport
steps: Read Mosiah 2:41 aloud together. Elder Bednar ended his talk with this promise from King Benjamin.
Check for understanding: each youth tells a partner, in one breath, what a covenant is and how it is sealed.
Elder Bednar gave no specific assignment in this talk, so let the youth choose their own. Show the act list. Each person writes one choice in their phone notes and sets a daily reminder.
Follow up: tell them you will ask next week what they did and what they noticed. Open next week's class with that question.

key_quotes.text: A covenant is a solemn promise—an enduring commitment between God and His sons and daughters.

Receiving this ratifying sealing by the Holy Ghost typically is not a one-time event; rather, it comes over time as we repent sincerely and consistently, honor our covenants, and yield our hearts unto God.
“Can the unrighteous exercise of moral agency by another person rob me of what God has promised?” The answer to this question is an emphatic no!
unrighteousness by one person cannot hinder or thwart the flow of God’s love, strength, and blessings to another person

scriptures.use: Read together in the segment The stamp. Have youth find the words Elder Bednar quotes and say in their own words what the Holy Spirit of Promise does.
Read after the board activity. Ask what it would look like for a teenager to walk in the ordinances of the Lord during a school week.
Read aloud together at the end. Ask each youth to pick the phrase that gives them the most hope.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Boyd K. Packer
aligned_quotes.text: To worthily receive them is the quest of a lifetime; to keep them thereafter is the challenge of mortality.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Sister Runia
aligned_quotes.text: Not understanding is not the same as not believing.

takeaways: A covenant is an enduring promise between God and me, and He sets the terms.
The Holy Ghost seals my covenants over time as I repent, honor them, and give my heart to God.
Nobody else's choices can cut me off from God's love, strength, and blessings.
act: Every night this week, repent of one specific thing in your prayer before you sleep.
During the sacrament on Sunday, put your phone away and think about one covenant promise you want to keep better.
Pick one of the board answers under REPENT, HONOR, or YIELD and do it each day until next class.
If someone's choices are weighing on you, read Mosiah 2:41 each morning and talk with a parent or leader you trust.
adapt: At home or with one or two youth: skip the acting and the teams. Read the passport story together, each write a twelve-word definition, and compare with Elder Bednar's.
Large class: run the twelve-word challenge in teams of four and let only three teams read aloud.
Only 15 minutes: do Will it get you in?, the passport story, the REPENT, HONOR, YIELD board, and the closing choice.

children.title: My Promises with Heavenly Father
children.big_idea: A covenant is a special promise with Heavenly Father; I can keep my promises, and the Holy Ghost helps me.
children.objective: Children will be able to say that a covenant is a special promise with Heavenly Father and name one way they will keep a promise this week.
prepare: Read Elder Bednar's talk, Sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise. This lesson teaches only its simplest truth; leave out everything about marriage and families.
Fold one sheet of paper in half for each child to make a small book, with a few spares. Bring crayons.
Bring a flashlight, a picture of the Savior, and six sheets of paper to lay on the floor as stepping stones.
Write one of these on each stepping stone, with a simple drawing: pray, be kind, tell the truth, say sorry, help, listen.

segments.name: Welcome and song
steps: Greet each child by name and invite a child to pray.
Sing The Holy Ghost or Keep the Commandments together.
Tell the children that today they will learn about special promises with Heavenly Father.

segments.name: What is a promise?
steps: Ask the first question below and listen to several answers.

Play a quick promise game. Say: I promise to clap three times. Then do it. Let three or four children make a small promise to the class, such as hopping twice or touching their toes, and keep it right away. Cheer each kept promise.
Teach the word covenant. Have the children say it with you three times: whisper it, say it, then say it while standing tall.
Tell them that Elder Bednar, an Apostle of Jesus Christ, taught what a covenant is. Read the first key quote. Explain that a covenant is a special promise between Heavenly Father and us.
questions: What is a promise?
How do you feel when someone keeps a promise to you?

segments.name: The traveler and his special book
steps: Give each child a folded paper book. Say it is their special book for today and ask them to take very good care of it.

Tell Elder Bednar's story simply while the children act it out: a man wanted to visit his family in a country far away. He packed his suitcase (pretend to pack). He flew on an airplane (arms out). He needed a special little book called a passport to go in. But he had not taken good care of it. It was stained and ripped. The helper at the gate could not let him in, and the man felt sad.
Ask the question below.

Say: our promises with Heavenly Father are even more special than a passport. We take good care of them by keeping them. If a child's paper is bent or torn, cheerfully give a fresh one and say that Heavenly Father helps us try again.
questions: What could the man have done to take good care of his special book?

segments.name: Walking home to Heavenly Father
steps: Lay the six stepping stones in a path across the room. Put the picture of the Savior at the end.
Tell the children that Elder Bednar shared the words of President Packer, who taught that life is a journey home to God. Read the first aligned quote.
One at a time or in pairs, the children walk the path holding their special book carefully. At each stone, the whole class calls out what is on it.
When each child reaches the picture, everyone says together: I keep my promises.
Ask the question below while the children sit down by the picture.
questions: Which stepping stone is something you can do today?

segments.name: The Holy Ghost helps me
steps: Dim the lights a little, keeping the room light enough to see safely. Turn on the flashlight and shine it along the stepping stones, one by one.

Say that Elder Bednar taught that the Holy Ghost is a messenger for Heavenly Father and Jesus. Read the second key quote. Like this light, the Holy Ghost helps us know what is true and right, and helps us feel that Heavenly Father is happy when we keep our promises.
Let two or three children take a turn shining the light on a stone while the class names what is on it.
Turn the lights up and ask the questions below.
questions: What does it feel like inside when you choose the right?
When could the Holy Ghost help you this week?

segments.name: My promise book
steps: Hand out crayons. Inside their special book, each child draws one way they will keep a promise this week. They may copy a stepping stone.
Walk around and ask each child to tell you about the drawing. This is your check that they understand.
Help them write on the cover: I keep my promises.

segments.name: Happy when we keep our promises
steps: Tell the children that Elder Bednar ended with a promise from King Benjamin in Mosiah 2:41: people who keep God's commandments are blessed and happy.
Bear a short testimony that Heavenly Father always keeps His promises and that the Holy Ghost will help them keep theirs.
Ask them to take their book home and put it where they will see it. Follow up: next week, begin by asking who kept the promise in their book and how it felt.

key_quotes.text: A covenant is a solemn promise
The Holy Ghost is the third member of the Godhead.
the blessed and happy state of those that keep the commandments of God

scriptures.use: In the last segment, tell the children in your own words that King Benjamin promised that those who keep God's commandments are blessed and happy. Older children can read the verse aloud.
Before the stepping-stone walk, tell the children this verse speaks of a promise to walk in the Lord's ways. Then walk the path together.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Boyd K. Packer
aligned_quotes.text: life is a homeward journey for all of us, back to the presence of God

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Oaks
aligned_quotes.text: I urge you to keep the commandments and be true to the covenants so many of you have made to guide you along the covenant path.

takeaways: A covenant is a special promise with Heavenly Father.
act: Do the thing you drew in your promise book every day this week.
When you pray at night, tell Heavenly Father one promise you kept today.
When you feel a warm, happy feeling after choosing the right, say quietly: thank You, Heavenly Father.

adapt.younger: Ages 3–7: keep each part short and moving. Use only three stepping stones (pray, be kind, say sorry) and walk the path twice, holding a helper's hand. Tell the traveler story in four sentences with big actions. Repeat I keep my promises after every activity, and let the children draw freely while you write the words for them.
adapt.older: Ages 8–11: have a child read Mosiah 2:41 aloud and another read Elder Bednar's definition of a covenant from the talk. Let older children lay out the stones, lead the walk, and hold the flashlight. Ask a harder question: why does keeping a promise every day matter more than making it once? You may add that Elder Bednar said hard things that are not our fault never spoil our promises with God.
